constraints.meaning: At least one number, at most 1,000.
constraints.impact: Even the O(n²) brute force (about 500,000 iterations) is fast enough here. Interviewers still expect the O(n) pass, because the same idea is needed for bigger inputs and for range-sum questions.

constraints.meaning: Values can be negative, zero or positive.
constraints.impact: A running sum is at most 1000 · 10⁶ = 10⁹ in absolute value. That is less than 2³¹ − 1 ≈ 2.1 · 10⁹, so int is enough. Negative values make the sum go down, so the result is not always increasing.

constraints.meaning: Each answer is the sum of all numbers up to and including index i.
constraints.impact: runningSum[i] = runningSum[i − 1] + nums[i]: every answer reuses the one before it. This is the prefix-sum pattern.

bruteForce.summary: for every index i, add nums[0] to nums[i] again from the start. The outer loop runs n times and the inner loop 1 + 2 + … + n times: O(n²) time. It never reuses the sum it already has.
